2.1.14.summary: Stratos updates itself, plans around real winds, and carries aircraft checklists to a paired phone.

features: Stratos updates itself: the app reads the published release manifest, names what changed, verifies the download against the published checksum and restarts into the new build.
Route weather in the planner: surface observations for the airports on the route, and winds aloft from the NOAA Aviation Weather Center worked into each leg's winds and cruise temperature.
Aircraft checklists with per-flight progress, using the same profile and the same ticks on the desktop app and a paired phone.
Phone pairing shows a QR code in Settings, so a phone opens the bridge URL without typing it.
improvements: The update centre in Settings reports the installed build, the latest release, the last check and the full release history, with a changelog viewer for every version.
The chart browser asks a provider registry for each region and says which publisher would be needed, instead of substituting a diagram Stratos has no right to display.
A paired phone can revoke its own access, and Settings can revoke one phone or all of them.
fixes: The sticky pilot sub-navigation no longer lets the page heading show through its tabs.
Long bridge values and data paths wrap instead of widening Settings on a phone.
ui: Settings groups the update state, release history and simulator details into one page that fits a phone at 390 px.
other: The release workflow generates the manifest from the tagged commits, publishes the notes as the release body, and reads the published assets back to verify them.
The chart browser check creates its screenshot folder, so it runs from a fresh checkout.

2.1.15.summary: Release notes written for readers, and every release now proves its own Windows update path.

features: Release notes can be written by hand for a version and are validated against the same schema the app reads, so an update describes what actually changed instead of repeating commit subjects.
improvements: Every published release now runs the Windows update test automatically: it installs the previous build, lets it update itself to the new one, and checks the installed version.
The release manifest also carries the hand-written notes for older versions, so a build that skips several releases still shows the full history.
